[2023 fall ms applied — problem 4]

Three fertilizers $\times$ three seed types, 45 plots (5 replicates per combination). ANOVA SS: Seed 16.962, Fertilizer 11.820, Seed:Fertilizer 47.949, Residuals 45.210. (1) Give the degrees of freedom. (2) Test that the fertilizer effect is the same regardless of seed type (no interaction). (3) Test that fertilizer has no effect, for every seed type.

response.text:
Let the fixed-effects two-way ANOVA model be

\[
Y_{ijk}=\mu+\alpha_i+\beta_j+(\alpha\beta)_{ij}+\varepsilon_{ijk},
\]

where \(i=1,2,3\) indexes seed type, \(j=1,2,3\) indexes fertilizer, and \(k=1,\dots,5\) indexes replicates. Assume the usual ANOVA assumptions: independent normal errors with common variance \(\sigma^2\).

There are \(3\times 3\times 5=45\) observations.

---

## (1) Degrees of freedom

For a \(3\times 3\) factorial design with 5 replicates per cell:

\[
df_{\text{Seed}}=3-1=2,
\]

\[
df_{\text{Fertilizer}}=3-1=2,
\]

\[
df_{\text{Seed:Fertilizer}}=(3-1)(3-1)=4,
\]

\[
df_{\text{Residual}}=3\cdot 3\cdot (5-1)=36,
\]

\[
df_{\text{Total}}=45-1=44.
\]

The ANOVA table is therefore:

| Source | SS | df | MS |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Seed | 16.962 | 2 | 8.481 |
| Fertilizer | 11.820 | 2 | 5.910 |
| Seed:Fertilizer | 47.949 | 4 | 11.987 |
| Residual | 45.210 | 36 | 1.256 |
| Total | 121.941 | 44 | |

The residual mean square is

\[
MSE=\frac{45.210}{36}=1.2558.
\]

---

## (2) Test for no interaction

We test

\[
H_0:(\alpha\beta)_{ij}=0 \quad \text{for all } i,j,
\]

against the alternative that at least one interaction term is nonzero.

The test statistic is

\[
F=\frac{MS_{\text{Seed:Fertilizer}}}{MSE}
=\frac{47.949/4}{45.210/36}.
\]

Compute:

\[
MS_{\text{Seed:Fertilizer}}=\frac{47.949}{4}=11.98725,
\]

so

\[
F=\frac{11.98725}{1.2558}=9.545.
\]

Under \(H_0\),

\[
F\sim F_{4,36}.
\]

The p-value is approximately

\[
p=P(F_{4,36}\ge 9.545)\approx 2.3\times 10^{-5}.
\]

Thus we strongly reject \(H_0\). There is very strong evidence of a seed-by-fertilizer interaction. Equivalently, the fertilizer effect is not the same across seed types.

---

## (3) Test that fertilizer has no effect for every seed type

The null hypothesis is that within each seed type, the mean response is the same for all fertilizers:

\[
H_0:\mu_{i1}=\mu_{i2}=\mu_{i3} \quad \text{for each } i=1,2,3.
\]

This is stronger than testing only the fertilizer main effect. It requires both no fertilizer main effect and no seed-by-fertilizer interaction. Therefore the appropriate numerator sum of squares is

\[
SS_{\text{Fertilizer}}+SS_{\text{Seed:Fertilizer}}
=11.820+47.949=59.769.
\]

The numerator degrees of freedom are

\[
df=(3-1)+(3-1)(3-1)=2+4=6.
\]

Thus the test statistic is

\[
F=\frac{(SS_{\text{Fertilizer}}+SS_{\text{Seed:Fertilizer}})/6}{MSE}
=\frac{59.769/6}{45.210/36}.
\]

Compute:

\[
\frac{59.769}{6}=9.9615,
\]

so

\[
F=\frac{9.9615}{1.2558}=7.932.
\]

Under \(H_0\),

\[
F\sim F_{6,36}.
\]

The p-value is approximately

\[
p=P(F_{6,36}\ge 7.932)\approx 1.7\times 10^{-5}.
\]

Thus we strongly reject \(H_0\). There is very strong evidence that fertilizer affects the response for at least one seed type.
